prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabling the delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved a concrete physical-chemical problem: how to entrap and deliver large polyanionic nucleic acids and release them in the cytosol. The solution rests on lipid self-assembly, pKa-controlled charge, and pH-triggered non-bilayer phase behaviour that drives endosomal escape. This is lipid colloid chemistry applied with rigor. It enabled the first siRNA drug and then the mRNA vaccines, and the evidence is clinical and independently confirmed at a scale few chemical discoveries reach. After hearing colleagues, I think the Vancouver trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden) offers the cleanest attribution chain. They worked out the early ionizable-lipid entrapment and formulation principles that later lipid optimisation (including Anderson's and Langer's lipidoid libraries and the MacLachlan-linked work) built on. It also draws support from several colleagues who rank it second or third (Aili, Chabes) and does not depend on a recent clinical milestone. Maturity is therefore stronger than for my opening first choice, B007, which three colleagues call possibly premature.
statement.case_against: Credit is spread across at least six people and several companies, and a three-person cap leaves out Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, whose lipidoid and lipid-optimisation work was decisive for later products. Patent disputes make priority hard to adjudicate from the scientific record. The 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA overlaps in application, so the Committee may judge that delivery is an engineering optimisation rather than a distinct chemical discovery. I also hold this view as a lipid physical chemist, so I may overrate the lipid phase-behaviour side of the story.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs and molecular glues first as a new pharmacological modality with a design-driven chemistry and many degraders in clinical trials, and ranks ionizable LNPs second.
responses.response: I agree on the conceptual originality of induced proximity and I rank B014 among my alternatives. But I part ways on timing and attribution. No degrader is approved, and the credit is split across two strands (PROTAC concept versus cereblon and molecular glues), so the three-person cap forces a choice between them that a single citation would hide. LNPs have the opposite profile, with proven global clinical use. I welcome Aili's second-place support for B060 and would hold the Committee to that.

responses.point: Chabes places B014 first and B060 third, noting that the 2023 Medicine prize recognized mRNA modification but not the delivery chemistry, and that Cullis is the core figure with many company-linked contributors.
responses.response: I share Chabes' reading that 2023 does not cover delivery, which answers Brzezinski's overlap worry in part. I differ on whether to narrow to Cullis plus Anderson. Madden and Hope co-developed the ionizable-lipid entrapment work in Vancouver and are central to the early papers. Dropping them for Anderson would favour later lipid screening over the founding formulation principles. I would keep the Vancouver trio, and I accept that Anderson and Langer's omission is a real cost.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first on mechanistic clarity and ranks B060 fifth, citing contested allocation, patent disputes and the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: I accept that B046 is the cleanest two-person case on the table, mature and mechanistically well understood, and I did not rank it. My concern is the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which Somfai and Zou treat as a minor issue but which makes B046 a closer sibling than a new concept. On B060, patent disputes are not a scientific ground for exclusion, and I would judge the case on who first established ionizable-lipid entrapment and pH-triggered release. The 2023 overlap is in application, not in the chemistry honoured.

responses.point: Zou ranks Buchwald and Hartwig first and says that the PROTAC prize looks slightly early because no approved degrader exists, while ranking B060 sixth because the chemistry credit is less clear.
responses.response: I agree that B014 is slightly early and use that argument against it. I do not agree that the chemistry credit for B060 is less clear. The pKa-dependent charge and non-bilayer lipid phase behaviour are physical-chemical principles with an identifiable origin in the Vancouver work. I concede that the formulation is less molecularly defined than a catalytic cycle, and that Zou's criterion of conceptual originality is harder to apply to an optimisation of lipid structures.

responses.point: Linke ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first as an unambiguous two-person credit with long-overdue recognition, and puts perovskites second.
responses.response: The attribution cleanliness of B027 is hard to match, and I take the point that it has had little recent recognition in computational chemistry. I placed it outside my own ranking only because I know soft-matter chemistry better than electronic-structure methods, which is a limit on my judgement. I would not block it, but I judge LNPs to have the larger demonstrated chemical impact.

uncertainties: How to divide credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, and whether the Vancouver trio is the right cut.
Whether the Committee treats LNP delivery as a distinct chemical discovery or as formulation optimisation following the 2023 Medicine prize.
Whether B007 phase separation will mature enough to displace this choice, given the contested physiological relevance of many condensates.
My recollection of detailed priority in the early ionizable-lipid papers comes from memory and is not verified.
statement.conflict_note: My research field (lipid self-assembly, membrane physical chemistry, lipid-protein co-assembly) overlaps strongly with B060 and, to a lesser extent, B007. I have no stated personal or institutional tie to any credited name in the provided profile, but the subject overlap may merit a note on potential recusal or disclosure. I also serve with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which is not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate that I can see.
